title: Grade 7 Math — Thu, Jun 12
description: Simple & Compound Interest — Day 4 of 5: CI compounded half-yearly and applications
subject: mathematics

questions.question: When CI is compounded half-yearly (twice a year), the rate per period is ___.
questions.explanation: Half-yearly means 2 periods per year. Rate per period = R/2.

questions.question: For CI compounded half-yearly for T years, the number of periods n = ___.
questions.explanation: Two periods per year × T years = 2T total compounding periods.

questions.question: P = ₹10000, R = 10% per year, compounded half-yearly for 1 year. Rate per half-year = ___.
P=₹10000, R=10%/yr, compounded half-yearly for 1 year. Periods = ___.
Compare half-yearly CI (₹1025) vs annual CI (₹1000) for P=₹10000, R=10%, T=1yr. Which is more?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly CI = ₹1025 > Annual CI = ₹1000. More frequent compounding = more interest.

questions.question: More frequent compounding means ___ interest earned.
questions.explanation: The more frequently interest is compounded (monthly > quarterly > half-yearly > annual), the more interest accumulates.

questions.question: A population of 1000 grows at 5% per year (compounded). After 2 years the population = ___.
The price of a machine is ₹20000. It depreciates at 10% per year (CI-style). After 2 years its value = ___.
The formula for depreciation (reduction in value) uses (1 − R/100) because ___.
questions.explanation: We subtract R/100 since the value is going DOWN each year.

questions.question: P = ₹5000, R = 12% per year, CI annually, T = 2 yr. (1.12)² = 1.2544. CI = ___.
